text: The slot holds the head `discriminant` for `tinyclip-39m-16` (shrinkage 0.03), fitted on `images/alachua-pre2025`, with 5467 species rows, and a bias a row. Every photo's vector (`images/alachua-2025.wasm-int8-per-channel`) went through `tools/fusion/fuse.py`, the reference of the page's arithmetic, with the slot's own files as the page reads them (half-precision rows). Settings: rule `mix`, t_kind 0.5, w_kind 0.7, alpha_prior 0.6. On 1803 tuning photos (val) the thresholds came out as name_at 0.82 and offer_at 0.98. On the 4197 test photos the kind of eye is right for 88.5% (87.5 to 89.5); the top species is right for 53.4% (51.9 to 55.0) and is among the first five for 75.1% (73.8 to 76.5). `person` was said for 0.00% of these photos and `none` for 0.02%; the set holds neither. The top species from fuse.py differs from a direct matrix computation on the same files for 0 photos. The kinds head is `kind rows fitted on the fitting photos and the extra set (every photo counts the same)`. With kind_at 0.51 (set on wildlife tuning photos and the extra set's tuning third), the page asserts a kind for 84.8% (83.7 to 85.9) of the wildlife test photos and is right for 95.0% (94.2 to 95.7) of those; for the 15.2% (14.1 to 16.3) where it is not sure, the true kind is among its three likeliest for 86.1% (83.4 to 88.6). On the 1240 test photos of people, cats, dogs, grazing animals and rooms (`images/coco-kinds.wasm-int8-per-channel`), the kind is right for 97.4% (96.5 to 98.2); the page asserts a kind for 95.5% (94.2 to 96.7) and is right for 98.9% (98.3 to 99.5) of those; where it is not sure the true kind is among its three likeliest for 94.6% (87.5 to 100.0). A species is named on 16.1% (14.1 to 18.2) of these photos. The slot needs: species.bias_url (build 7 of the page); kinds.bias (build 7 of the page); fusion.rule mix (build 7 of the page); fusion.kind_at (the build of the page that has the answer `not sure`).
